newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mayne confident on EBIT for year.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mayne confident on EBIT for year.

text.p: Australian transport group Mayne Nickless Ltd said on Thursday that it was confident it would meet its plans for earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) for the full financial year to June 30.

Mayne earlier reported a net profit of A$43.14 million for the six months to December 31, down from A$50.06 million a year earlier. Earnings before interest and tax slipped 0.7 percent to A$101.4 million. Sales eased 6.3 percent to A$1.38 billion.
"Our underlying EBIT has improved year on year, but for the latest half year we've booked higher goodwill charges due to an accounting standard change," managing director Bob Dalziel said.

"Whilst reductions in our corporate overheads have been initiated, these have not been implemented as quickly as we expected, and have lagged behind the business divestments and restructuring that have occurred," he said.
"I remain optimistic, however, that overall EBIT plans for the year will be met," Dalziel said.

Dalziel said the result was in line with the company's operating plans and reflected the restructuring of its European and Australian contract logistics and Australian time critical express groups which he said would continue through 1997.
"Importantly, we are encouraged by the early signs from the restructuring of the Australian time critical express business," he said.
"As a consequence of this work we determined late last year to pursue a "get big" strategy in our selected markets."
Dalziel said Mayne believed that significant size in each of the geographic markets in which it operated was fundamental.
"Logistics in Europe is highly competitive and we have observed that there is a consolidation of the market taking place," he said.
"This is reinforced by our investigation of possible acquisitions in France. In addition, out customers are increasingly looking for pan-European solutions and larger networks," he said.
"In November 1996 management, therefore, decided to explore all options ranging from acquisitions to the identification of a party who is pursuing growth in European logistics," he said.
"To date we are encouraged by our assessments that we will be able to profitably participate in the consolidation process."
Among the divisions, Health Care of Australia had revenue of A$342 million, up 50 percent on the prior corresponding period.

"The increase was partly attributable to a full half contribution from businesses that were part of Australian Medical Enterprises which the company acquired in October 1995, including St George Private Hospital in Sydney," Mayne said.

Earnings before interest and tax totalled A$44 million, up 48 percent from a year earlier. Time critical express reported revenue of A$598 million, down three percent, largely due to the strength of the Australian dollar, Mayne said.
EBIT fell 15 percent to A$24.66 million.
Contract logistics reported revenue of A$444 million, down one percent, also due the dollar's strength, it said.
EBIT was flat at A$38 million.
Mayne also announced that Optus Communications, in which it has a 25 percent stake, had earnings before tax of A$59 million for the period, up from A$7 million a year earlier.
Mayne plans to float off or sell the stake.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
